newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Softer Australian dlr ends above support zone.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Softer Australian dlr ends above support zone.

text.p: The Australian dollar spent an uneventful day trading a narrow range after overnight selling had seen it fall through support, with talk of a options strangle limiting the currency's movement.
Traders said the market was reasonably quiet ahead of U.S. CPI data later today and even Japanese GDP data released late in local trade had little impact.
By 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT) the Australian dollar was trading near its lows for the day at US$0.7962/67 from an early US$0.7970/75 and was down on Thursday's close of US$0.7988/93.

Traders said after data on Thursday showed a rise in the unemployment rate to 8.8 percent, offshore sentiment on the increased prospect of another local rate cut had seen some selling that continued in local trade this morning.

"There was a little bit of interest pushing it lower this morning," one trader said. "It pushed back higher through US$0.7975 but ran into local selling that may have been attributable to bond selling."
The US$0.7980/85 support level through which the unit fell was now fairly good resistance, but the US$0.7955/60 level was expected to provide robust support, traders said.

A options strangle was rumoured to be set at US$0.7950/8050, and due to expire on Monday afternoon. Asian buying was seen as protecting that position on any dips. However, not all traders were convinced of the strangle position's existence.

Traders did agree that US$0.7950 was an important level for the Australian dollar, and said the market may be slightly long above that given that protection of the options strangle was expected to see that level hold.
A break of US$0.7950 would set off stop losses, and "if we break US$0.7945, it will travel a lot further," the trader said.
On the crosses, the Australian dollar was also softer over the course of the day.
Even the annoucement of a 30 billion yen two year samurai bond issue failed to keep the unit on a firmer footing.

The Australian dollar closed at 87.63/73 yen from an early 87.69/79 and a local Thursday close of 88.00/10. In trade weighted terms, the unit closed at 58.7, level with its open but down a touch on its previous close of 58.8.
